speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The incident was extremely painful for all of us in the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) family.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They continue to be missed and will be remembered as caring and good-natured colleagues.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A third officer, Engineering Manager Mr Low Yin Choon, suffered third-degree burns during the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: He has since recovered and returned to work.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Following the incident, NEA provided the families of all three officers with care and support, covered all medical expenses and provided workplace injury compensation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Till this day, NEA remains in contact with the families of the two late officers.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The charges against NEA and its officers are serious.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I had indicated, on the day the charges were filed, that I would be making a Statement in Parliament about the incident and charges.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In addition, Members have asked questions: Ms Poh Li San asked about how NEA has strengthened its workplace safety practices and culture; Mr Melvin Yong asked about measures put in place to ensure such an incident does not recur.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These are important questions which I will address.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, as the case is currently before the Courts, I seek Members' understanding that what I can share today will be limited, so as not to prejudice the ongoing judicial proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, I will not be able to go into details of the incident itself, or what contributed to the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In my Statement, I will cover, briefly, the incident and how it was handled by MSE and NEA; NEA's response to the charges; and NEA's ongoing commitment to workplace safety.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Most of this information is already in the public domain.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Induced Draft Fan is used to extract gases from the incineration process for discharge via the chimney and is about two metres wide.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Kwok Yeow Wai, Mr Wee Eng Leng and Mr Low Yin Choon from the Electrical Maintenance Branch obtained permission from the control room to troubleshoot the electrical fault.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Kwok, Mr Wee and Mr Low were the three most senior officers in the Electrical Maintenance Branch.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The troubleshooting led them to an electrical switch room.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Kwok died at the scene and Mr Wee was seriously injured.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Wee succumbed to his injuries three days later.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Low was also injured in the explosion, but has recovered and returned to work.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I will now speak about how NEA responded in the immediate aftermath of the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, what was done to ensure safety at the Tuas Incineration Plant and other incineration plants.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, what was done to investigate the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Immediately after the incident, Tuas Incineration Plant stopped receiving waste for incineration and was safely shut down.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On 27 September 2021, NEA was issued a Stop Work Order by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) to cease any process or works in relation to electrical servicing and maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: During the period of the Stop Work Order, NEA engineering officers carried out and completed comprehensive checks on machinery and reviewed all safety procedures at the plant.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Extensive checks and tests were also conducted by an external licensed electrical engineer.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA did likewise at Tuas South Incineration Plant.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA also notified private operators of incineration plants about the incident and requested them to review their safety procedures and equipment.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With MOM's clearance, Tuas Incineration Plant resumed partial operations on 13 October 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The waste that had been stored in the bunker from before the incident was then incinerated, but the plant did not receive new waste.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Incineration of the waste in the bunker was necessary to prevent the build-up of potentially flammable gas from the decomposition of waste.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Stop Work Order was eventually lifted by MOM on 24 November 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Tuas Incineration Plant had been in operation since 1986.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With the commencement of operations at TuasOne Waste-To-Energy Plant, which was developed to replace the Tuas Incineration Plant while catering for growth in Singapore's waste treatment capacity, NEA stopped operations at the Tuas Incineration Plant in February 2022, after 36 years of service, as planned.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Plant was eventually decommissioned in July 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: During the plant's 36 years of operations, there were no other serious or fatal work injuries at the plant.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In parallel with these safety measures, investigations were also carried out immediately after the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MOM, the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) and other technical agencies carried out their independent investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA also convened an internal Investigation Panel to ascertain the events which led to the incident, identify the possible causes and recommend additional measures to prevent the recurrence of such an incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It was chaired by a Group Director in NEA who had experience in the operations of incineration plants but was not managing such plants at the time.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The other three members were two Divisional Directors from the Ministry and NEA, and a former General Manager of the Tuas South Incineration Plant.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA also engaged an external technical expert to provide an independent review of the affected equipment and to advise the panel on the likely cause of the localised explosion.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Panel reported to the then-Chief Executive Officer of NEA.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Panel's findings were shared with the NEA board and the Ministry.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The findings were also shared with MOM investigators.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MOM has since concluded its investigation of the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Two senior officers in NEA have also been charged.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA is studying its charge in consultation with its legal counsel.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The two senior officers charged have been re-deployed to non-operational roles.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is important that we let the proceedings take its course and not come to any premature conclusion.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I will next cover the measures which have been put in place at NEA's incineration plant to ensure that such incidents do not recur and how NEA has strengthened its workplace safety practices and culture.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will address the questions filed by Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Poh Li San.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With the benefit of information obtained from its investigations, NEA's internal Investigation Panel made recommendations to strengthen the plant's work system and processes involving high voltage works.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I am not able to detail the specific recommendations due to the ongoing Court proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA also shared the recommendations with waste incineration plants that are privately operated, for their own process safety reviews.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Workplace safety is a continuous journey and it is important that we learn the lessons from each incident to make our systems and operations even safer and prevent recurrence of a similar incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Having covered the measures that were put in place shortly after the incident, I will now turn to how NEA is strengthening its workplace safety practices and culture, in a broader sense.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA is currently undertaking an operational review of its waste management facilities, which includes not just Tuas South Incineration Plant, but also other facilities, such as Semakau Landfill.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is part of a broader set of operational reviews to strengthen operational excellence, safety and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This ensures that NEA responds effectively to changes in the operating environment.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As part of the operational review for waste management facilities, NEA has appointed an External Advisory Panel (EAP), comprising senior industry leaders who have had experience managing large facilities and operations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The EAP is advising NEA on ways to strengthen operations and safety at its waste management facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA is also in the process of engaging consultants to undertake a technical review of existing operational processes and controls, which includes but is not limited to safety.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA has also taken steps to further strengthen workplace safety and health (WSH), taking reference from guidelines and best practices issued by the WSH Council.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: After the charges were filed, NEA also called an organisation-wide Safety Time Out to reaffirm its commitment to safety.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: During this week-long Safety Time Out, NEA re-assessed its WSH practices and work processes and NEA senior management conducted additional safety walkabouts and held discussions with officers on ways to further improve WSH.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These efforts were over and above regular WSH activities and served as opportunities to re-emphasise the importance of WSH.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA is also in the process of seeking external validation of its WSH practices through the bizSAFE Level 3 Risk Management Audit, which will take place later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In terms of governance at the board level, the NEA board was restructured last year to include a dedicated Risk Committee to oversee and manage key enterprise risks, including workplace safety which is a top priority for NEA.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Key enterprise risks were previously overseen by the Audit Committee, which reported to the board.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The formation of a Risk Committee is part of NEA's efforts to continually strengthen the governance of its risk management.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The localised explosion at Tuas Incineration Plant in 2021 was a painful chapter for NEA and the MSE family.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As I have set out in my Statement, NEA has implemented measures to prevent similar incidents from taking place.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: More broadly, as part of its continuous journey of improvement, NEA has strengthened WSH at its waste management facilities and across the entire organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The charge faced by NEA is a serious one.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Two of its officers have also been charged.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA has implemented all recommendations made by the internal Investigation Panel following the incident and strengthened its workplace safety culture and practices.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It would be premature to comment on the Court’s decision and the impact of the decision.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In response to some questions raised earlier for an MOM Parliamentary Question, I would like to add that WSH is one of NEA's key corporate key performance indicators (KPIs).

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is also taken into consideration for performance assessment and bonuses.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA has a dedicated WSH team supporting senior management to strengthen WSH culture and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Across NEA's premises and facilities, there are also WSH committees and appointment holders that oversee and manage WSH risks in the organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to focus on and emphasise the importance of building a collective and strong WSH culture.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The charges against NEA and its two senior officers are now before the Courts and going forward, they will be addressed as the legal process runs its course.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In the meantime, NEA and all our officers will continue to carry out their duties in service of Singapore and our people.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I urge all of us to play our part to ensure WSH, so that every worker can return home safely to their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Two senior NEA engineers lost their lives and another was seriously injured.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MOM, SCDF and other technical agencies concurrently carried out independent investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA also convened an internal Investigation Panel, which recommended additional measures to prevent the recurrence of such an incident.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The charges against NEA and its senior officers are serious.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Workplace safety is a continuous journey and remains a top priority for my Ministry and statutory boards, including NEA, to keep our operational and frontline workers safe.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I will now take clarifications from the Members.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will now have clarifications on the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members can certainly seek clarifications by way of asking questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I seek Member's understanding to keep your clarifications clear and concise.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Likewise, I will make the same request to Minister when she responds to these clarifications.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: And the second question is, what are the types of assistance that have been rendered to the families of the three affected staff?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The response to the first question is, definitely, yes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As I have stated in my speech earlier on, we have been keeping our other operators informed as and when we undertake reviews.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Obviously, the families had suffered, very regrettably, deep losses; and our colleagues had been long-time colleagues with these two officers as well.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Was there a proper risk assessment done for such plants and is it a requirement by NEA, even for the privately-run incineration plant?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If not, will NEA be appointing dedicated, trained WSH officers for all such facilities?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I acknowledge Senior Minister of State Zaqy's earlier response that beyond having a singular person looking at WSH within an organisation, we should also place some responsibility on individuals with oversight of the workplace or the worksite; so, he cited examples of project managers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, I would like to ask if the key managers overseeing such incineration plants are trained in workplace safety and safety risk assessments?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If not, will NEA send them for the proper WSH training?
